column2: The Great Bastion Besieged

The hordes of the Northern Wastes have come south in numbers not seen in an age, and hurl themselves against the Great Bastion. Every soldier the Dragon Throne can spare is on the wall, the Silk Road is all but closed, and the sky over the north burns with the light of the Ruinous Powers.
§Y*§! The value of the Silk Road is reduced by §R50%§!

column2: Ogre Raids

Ogre tribes have come down out of the Mountains of Mourning to eat their way through the western provinces of Cathay. The garrisons of the frontier are fighting them valley by valley, and the caravans of the Silk Road travel at their peril.
§Y*§! The value of the Silk Road is reduced by §R50%§!

column2: War Beneath the Earth

Clan Eshin and the other clans of the Under-Empire are gnawing at Cathay from below. Wells turn foul, officials die in their beds, and whole storehouses of jade vanish overnight down holes that were not there the day before.

column2: The Great Bastion no longer shakes under the hordes of the north
The Ogre tribes have gone back to the Mountains of Mourning
The war beneath Cathay has gone quiet
The Dragon Sends Aid

Sails have been sighted, and then banners: red silk and gold dragons. The [offmap_cathay.GetShortName] has heard that its children in the west are beset, and an army of the Dragon Throne has come ashore at [Root.Capital.GetName] to fight under my command until the war is won.
Glory to the Dragon Throne!
An army of §Y4,500§! Cathayan soldiers joins you until the war ends (§Y6,000§! if Cathay is in a Golden Age).

Merchants on the Silk Road report that [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has sent an army west to defend the Cathayan colonists of [From.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. The Dragon Throne does not forget its own, however far from home they have settled.
Settlers from Cathay

A fleet of junks has arrived from the east, carrying farmers, craftsmen and scribes sent by the Dragon Throne to strengthen its colonies. They bring seed, tools, and a chest of silver from the imperial treasury.
Settle them near [Root.Capital.GetName].
A Demand from the Dragon Throne

An envoy of [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has come to my court with a scroll sealed in jade. The Dragon Throne demands that I hand over [cathay_hunted_exile.GetBestName], who fled the justice of the Dragon Throne and now lives under my roof. The envoy did not say what will happen if I refuse. He did not need to.
Hand [cathay_hunted_exile.GetFirstName] over to the envoy.
My guests are under my protection.

Word has come that [cathay_hunted_exile.GetBestName], who fled the justice of the Dragon Throne, has been found dead. Nobody saw the killers come or go. In the bazaars along the Silk Road they say that [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has very long arms.
The east does not forget.
Hidden Blades

They came at night, quiet as cats, with blades of black jade. My guards cut down two of them before they reached my chamber. None carried anything that names a master, but I know who sent them. The Dragon Throne has not forgiven me.
Double the guard.
Cathayan Aid Sent
Cathayan Settlers Sent
Hunted by Cathay (Cooldown)
Hunted by Cathay
Agents of the Dragon Throne have tried to kill this character, and will try again.
Cathayan Settlers
Farmers, craftsmen and scribes sent by the Dragon Throne have settled here.
Learning of Cathay
Scrolls, star charts and engineers carried off from Cathay are spreading new ideas through this realm.

The End Times have reached the east. Out of the Northern Wastes a horde beyond counting has fallen on the Great Bastion, the wall that has guarded Cathay since the first Dragon Emperor. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has called every army in the empire north to hold it.

Ogre tribes have come down out of the Mountains of Mourning and are eating their way through the western provinces of Cathay. The frontier garrisons are fighting them valley by valley, and the caravans on the Silk Road are being plundered.

Strange news from Cathay: wells turning foul, officials dying in their beds, whole storehouses of jade vanishing overnight. The Cathayans say ratmen are tunnelling beneath their cities, and [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has sent soldiers down into the dark after them.
Troubling news.

The Great Bastion has held. After years of slaughter on the wall, the hordes of the north have broken and fled back into the Wastes, leaving their dead piled at its foot. Cathay has paid dearly for the victory and the empire is restless, but the Dragon Throne still stands.

The northern hordes have broken through the Great Bastion and put the northern provinces of Cathay to the torch before they were driven out. Fields lie burnt and granaries empty, and famine is spreading through the empire.

The unthinkable has happened. The Great Bastion has fallen and the hordes of the north have stormed the capital. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetBestName], a warlord of the Ruinous Powers, now sits on the Dragon Throne. Of the Dragon Emperor nothing is known, except that his body was not found.

The Dragon Emperor has returned. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetBestName] came down on the capital in his true form, and the Chaos warlord who had taken his throne was burnt where he stood. The servants of the Ruinous Powers are being hunted out of Cathay province by province.
The Ogre tribes have been driven back into the Mountains of Mourning. The western garrisons have rebuilt their forts, and the caravans are moving again.

Rather than fight the Ogres valley by valley, the Dragon Throne has paid them to go home, and paid well. The tribes have gone back to the Mountains of Mourning laden with silver, and the Ogre Kingdoms of the west are spending it already.
The Ogres have finally gone home, but not before eating the western granaries of Cathay bare. Famine is spreading through the provinces they passed through.
The war beneath Cathay is over. The tunnels under its cities have been flooded and sealed, and the ratmen burnt out of their warrens. The empire is calm again.
Before they were driven out, the ratmen poisoned the wells of Cathay. A terrible plague is now spreading through its cities.
The ratmen have gone back underground, and a great deal of Cathay's jade and warpstone has gone with them. The Under-Empire is richer for it, and the Cathayan court is looking for someone to blame.
Assault the Dragon Throne

Beyond the eastern edge of the world lies Grand Cathay, ruled by a dragon who thinks himself eternal. The Dark Gods say otherwise. March on the Great Bastion and put a champion of the Ruinous Powers on the Dragon Throne.
An adult, unlanded member of your dynasty at court will lead the claim. If there is none, a champion of your dynasty will step forward. If the war is won, §Ythe claimant becomes Emperor of Cathay§!.
Launch an Expedition into Cathay

Grand Cathay is the richest empire in the world, and its riches lie just beyond the eastern edge of the map. You have no wish to sit on the Dragon Throne, but there is gold, slaves, influence and learning to be had there for anyone strong enough to take it.
You will choose what the expedition is after: §Yplunder§!, §Yslaves§!, §Yinfluence§! or §Yknowledge§!.
An Expedition East

My captains are gathered and my armies are ready to cross the eastern edge of the world. Before we march, they want to know what we are going for. Cathay has more of everything than any realm in the west, and we cannot carry it all home.
Gold, jade and silk!
Slaves, as many as we can drive home.
Force the Dragon Throne to deal with us.
Their scholars, their star charts, their secrets.
On second thought, not yet.
If the war is won: §G+4000§! gold, prestige, and a Cathayan jian and dragon amulet. Cathay will not forget.
If the war is won: §G+1500§! gold, and Cathayan slaves put to work in up to four of your provinces for 20 years. Cathay will not forget.
If the war is won: §G+2500§! Grace, favoured trade with Cathay for 50 years, the Jade Dragon, and Cathay is forced to open its borders.
If the war is won: faster technology spread for 50 years, a Cathayan water clock, and two Cathayan scholars join your court.

[From.GetBestName] has marched on Grand Cathay to carry off its people in chains. The armies of [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] are gathering to meet [From.GetHerHim].

[From.GetBestName] has marched on Grand Cathay to force the Dragon Throne to treat with [From.GetHerHim] as an equal. The armies of [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] are gathering to meet [From.GetHerHim].

[From.GetBestName] has marched on Grand Cathay in search of its libraries, its observatories and its engineers. The armies of [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] are gathering to meet [From.GetHerHim].
The expedition of [From.GetBestName] has come home from Cathay with wagons groaning under jade, silk and silver. The Dragon Throne is said to have sworn vengeance.
The expedition of [From.GetBestName] has come home from Cathay driving long columns of captives before it. The Dragon Throne is said to have sworn vengeance.
The expedition of [From.GetBestName] has won its war, and the Dragon Throne has been forced to open its borders and to receive [From.GetHerHis] envoys with honour.
The expedition of [From.GetBestName] has come home from Cathay with scrolls, star charts and scholars. What they know will soon be known across [From.PrimaryTitle.GetName].

[From.GetBestName] has turned the hordes of the Ruinous Powers east, against the Great Bastion itself. At their head rides [invasion_of_cathay_claimant.GetBestName], who has sworn to cast down the Dragon Emperor and sit on the Dragon Throne in the name of the Dark Gods.
May the Bastion hold.

Cathay is forced to §YOpen§! its borders.
Two Cathayan scholars join your court.
